reference_sql:
SELECT o.order_id, s.city
FROM orders o
JOIN stores s ON s.store_id = o.store_id
WHERE o.order_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-03-03 00:00:00' AND o.order_ts < TIMESTAMP '2025-03-04 00:00:00'
alternatives: SELECT o.order_id, s.city FROM stores s JOIN orders o ON o.store_id = s.store_id WHERE CAST(o.order_ts AS DATE) = DATE '2025-03-03'
SELECT o.order_id, s.city FROM orders o JOIN stores s ON s.store_id = o.store_id AND o.order_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-03-03 00:00:00' AND o.order_ts < TIMESTAMP '2025-03-04 00:00:00'

other_way.sql: SELECT o.order_id, s.city FROM orders o JOIN stores s ON s.store_id = o.store_id AND o.order_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-03-03 00:00:00' AND o.order_ts < TIMESTAMP '2025-03-04 00:00:00'
other_way.tradeoff: Putting the date test in ON gives the same rows in an inner join, but WHERE shows the filter more plainly.
